prerequisites: Fluid Mechanics (e.g., Fluid Mechanics I, Introduction to Fluid Mechanics, Introduction to Fluidomechanical Engineering, or similar)

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the Industrial Technical Engineer profession.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, work plans and other similar works.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.

syllabus_topics: Block I. Generalities.
Topic 1. Thermal Machines and Engines. Generalities.

Concept of a thermal machine. Internal combustion and external combustion thermal engines. Distinction between thermal machine and thermal engine. Efficiency of thermal engines. Cogeneration. Fields of application of thermal engines.
Topic 2. Processes in Compressible Fluids

Summary of basic concepts: Thermodynamic processes of importance in the study of thermal machines and engines. Principles and equations governing the behavior of compressible flows. Thermodynamic properties of ideal gas mixtures. The Carnot Factor. Maximum efficiency of thermal engines. Concepts of speed of sound, Mach number and shock wave. Expansion and compression in ducts, nozzles and diffusers. Expansion in convergent ducts. Fluid behavior in a convergent-divergent duct. Evaluation of losses in nozzles and diffusers.
Topic 3. Fundamentals of Combustion

Phenomena involved in the combustion process. Governing equations. Stoichiometric reaction. Complete combustion with excess air. Mechanism of the combustion reaction. Incomplete combustion. Energy balance in combustion processes. Adiabatic flame temperature. Classification of combustion processes. Autoignition of the air-fuel mixture. Premixed flames. Deflagration. Detonation. Diffusion flames.
Topic 4. Fuels Used in Thermal Systems and Engines

Classification of fuels. Fossil fuels. Characteristics and applications. Alternative or substitute fuels. Characteristics and applications. Fuel properties related to composition. Physical properties of fuel. Chemical properties of fuel. Fuel behavior in relation to combustion. Most important properties of main fuels.
Block II. Volumetric Machines and Engines.
Topic 5. Generalities of Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines

Components and basic processes of a reciprocating internal combustion engine. Classification of ICEs. Evolution of the working fluid during engine operation. p-alpha diagram and indicator diagram. Engine characteristic curves. Constant volume equivalent air cycles. Limited pressure equivalent air cycle.
Topic 6. The Combustion Process in Spark Ignition Engines and Compression Ignition Engines

Types of combustion in reciprocating internal combustion engines. Combustion in SI engines. Basic concepts of combustion in SI engines. Factors influencing the determination of ignition advance. Abnormal combustion in SI engines. Detonating combustion and surface ignition. Combustion in CI engines. Main functions of injection in CI engines. Micromixing and macromixing. Phases of combustion. Factors influencing the p-alpha diagram. Dual fuel engines. Stratified charge engines. HCCI combustion engines.
Topic 7. Volumetric Compressors

Definition and classification. Reciprocating compressors: Principle of operation. Thermodynamic analysis. p-V diagram. Volumetric efficiency. Displacement selection. Isothermal efficiency. Multi-stage compression. Types and mechanical configurations. Fields of application. Diaphragm reciprocating compressors. Control methods for reciprocating compressors. Rotary compressors. Screw compressors: Principle of operation. p-V diagrams. Types. Advantages and disadvantages. Vane compressors. Principle of operation and types. Scroll compressors: Principle of operation. Roots compressors: Principle of operation. p-V diagrams. Fields of application of rotary compressors. Blowers and vacuum pumps.
Block III. Power Plants Based on Gas Turbines and Steam Turbines
Topic 8. Gas Turbines for Mechanical Power Generation (Part one)

Types of installations. Thermodynamic analysis of ideal air cycles. Selection of thermodynamic cycle parameters for a gas turbine in cases of: simple cycle, regenerative simple cycle, compound cycle, regenerative compound cycle. Gas turbine behavior at the design point.
Topic 9. Gas Turbines for Mechanical Power Generation (Part two)

Design criteria for gas turbine installations. Evolution in design and state of the art of gas turbines. Power regulation of industrial gas turbines. Cogeneration with gas turbines. Principle of operation of aviation gas turbines. Turbojet engine. Mechanical schematic and principle of operation. Description of the combustion process in gas turbines. Pollution control systems in gas turbines.
Topic 10. Power Plants Based on Steam Turbines

Main components of power plants based on steam turbines. Rankine cycle. Influence of thermodynamic parameters of steam cycle power plants. Influence of steam pressure at turbine inlet. Influence of live steam temperature. Influence of condensation pressure. Steam cycles used in large steam power plants. Steam cycles with inter-reheating. Regenerative steam cycles. Steam turbines in industrial uses. Cogeneration in steam cycle plants. Turbines with intermediate bleed. Back-pressure turbines. Steam generators. Definition and classification of boilers. Classification of boilers. Description of boilers. Processes occurring in boilers. Parameters and fundamentals of boiler design.
Topic 11. Gas-Steam Combined Cycles

Combined cycles generalities: Classification. Thermodynamic fundamentals. General scheme of a gas and steam turbine combined cycle plant and types of assembly. Characteristics of gas turbines and their influence on combined cycle behavior. Influence of compression ratio. Influence of turbine inlet temperature. Influence of exhaust temperature. Types of cycles used. Heat recovery steam generator. Definition. Types of boilers. Relevant parameters. Irreversibilities. Characteristics of the steam cycle and its influence on combined cycle behavior. Influence of pressure at different levels. Influence of temperature. Types of cycles and configurations used.
Block IV. Thermal Turbomachinery
Topic 12. General Basic Concepts of Thermal Turbomachinery

Fundamental equation of turbomachines. Analysis of energy exchange in turbomachines. Structure of thermal turbomachines. Classification of turbomachines. Application of the above equations and concepts to turbines and compressors. Types of stages: axial reaction and impulse turbomachines. Axial turbocompressors. Radial turbomachines. Centripetal turbines. Centrifugal turbocompressors. Criteria used to define turbomachine efficiency. Origin of losses in turbomachines. Internal power and effective power.
Topic 13. Axial Turbines

Fields of application of axial turbines and centripetal turbines. Parameters defining the geometry of a blade cascade and the flow through it. Relationship between machine geometry and velocity triangles. Parameters defining the velocity diagram in a turbine stage. Factors on which losses and efficiency in axial turbine stages depend. Importance of the velocity diagram in machine pre-design. Optimal values of parameters characterizing the shape of the velocity diagram.
Topic 14. Axial Compressors

Parameters on which losses in axial compressors depend. Loss correlations. Optimal values of parameters characterizing the shape of the velocity diagram. Reason why multiple stages are necessary in axial compressors. Considerations on the design of axial turbomachines. Comparison between axial, centrifugal and volumetric compressors.

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as: Face-to-face exam grade + 0.1 * Average Continuous Assessment Tests (PEC) grade + 0.6 points for practical sessions. To pass the face-to-face exam, a score of 5 out of 10 or higher is required, with at least 5 out of 10 in the theoretical part and at least 3 out of 10 in the problem part; otherwise, the exam grade is 'NO APTO'. PECs are voluntary and only contribute if face-to-face exam minimums are met and the average PEC grade is >= 6, with a maximum contribution of 1 point to the final grade (0.1 times the PEC average grade). Face-to-face practical sessions are mandatory for students with a face-to-face exam grade >= 4.4 and contribute 0.6 points to the final grade if attendance is met and the qualification obtained is >= 7 out of 10, and must be approved (>5) to pass the course.
